capitals.name: Sarmizegetusa Regia
capitals.note: 'Trajan reduced the Dacian capital Sarmizegetusa to ruins in 106 AD' (Decebalus page). [Fix 2026-10-19: from 85 to match the new start; the pages give no capital for Duras's years, so Sarmizegetusa is assumed for 85-86.]

rulers.name: Duras
rulers.note: Duras is the Decebalus page's predecessor ('Decebalus was crowned king after the ageing Duras abdicated'; 'In 86 King Duras ordered a more vigorous attack south into Moesia'); the Dacia page's infobox lists 'Duras 69-87'. The dossier starts in 85, the first year a page dates his state's acts, so the reign is clipped to 85-86; Decebalus's infobox reign starts in 87.

rulers.name: Decebalus
rulers.note: 'Decebalus ruled the Dacians between AD 87 and 106'; crowned after King Duras abdicated; client king of Rome after 89; died by suicide in 106 rather than be captured.

correction.text: Roman Dacia's land (Transylvania, Banat, Oltenia): Dacia Traiana, the part of Decebalus's kingdom that Trajan annexed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (reviewer eu-04-x fix: the life starts under Duras in 85, not at Decebalus's accession): none of the pages gives the kingdom's extent in Decebalus's day (the Decebalus page lists only Banat; the Trajan page says the 'conquered half (southern) of Dacia' became the province and the northern part 'remained free'). Roman Dacia's region (Transylvania, Banat, Oltenia, 134 thousand km2) is the land certainly Dacian and annexed in 106; the Free Dacians' land beyond, and Muntenia, are not drawn. After 102 Decebalus had lost 'some territories in the vicinity of the Danube' (Decebalus page), which are not drawn either. No area on any page. The Decebalus page says Duras 'claimed authority over all Dacian territory'; no page gives his extent, so the same Roman Dacia region is drawn from 85.

ledger.note: 85: the Dacian kingdom under King Duras raids Moesia. 'In 85 AD the Dacian army began minor raids upon the heavily fortified Roman province of Moesia' and 'In 86 King Duras ordered a more vigorous attack south into Moesia' (Decebalus page); Duras 'claimed authority over all Dacian territory'. The dossier starts here, with the first act the pages date for the state, not at Decebalus's accession in 87 (a change of ruler, see the rename); the Dacia page's infobox lists Duras at 69-87 and the kingdom 'Established: c. 168 BC', but no page gives the kingdom's extent or any act before 85. The land is the researcher's reading. [Fix 2026-10-19: was 87 'Decebalus becomes king'.]

87: Decebalus is crowned king. 'Fuscus was killed, and Decebalus was crowned king after the ageing Duras abdicated' (Decebalus page; infobox 'Predecessor: Duras', 'Reign: 87-106 AD'); the Dacia page's infobox ends Duras at 87. The state and its land continue under Decebalus.

region.text: Roman Dacia's land (Transylvania, Banat, Oltenia): Dacia Traiana, the part of Decebalus's kingdom that Trajan annexed

ledger.note: 88: the Romans defeat the Dacians near Tapae. 'Tettius Julianus defeated the Dacians in a battle near Tapae' in 88 (Decebalus page); the Dacian raids on Moesia began in 85 and in 86 Duras ordered 'a more vigorous attack south into Moesia', i.e. before Decebalus's reign (87), so the contest starts in the first campaign inside Decebalus's reign. The page does not say Rome held ground. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the Dacian raids of 85 and the attack of 86 into Moesia are in the war record (wars/0) and not a contest: the pages do not say the Dacians held ground in Moesia, and Fuscus's defeat at Tapae has no year on them.]

ledger.note: 89: Domitian makes peace. The Romans 'were obligated to make peace following the defeat of Domitian by the Marcomanni'; Decebalus became a 'king client to Rome' (Dacia page); Decebalus page: Domitian 'agreed to pay large sums (eight million sesterces) in annual tribute to the Dacians' and sent a royal diadem and engineers. The Decebalus page does not date the peace; the Dacia page ties it to the Marcomanni defeat of Domitian, which the Marcomanni page dates to 89.

region.text: Roman Dacia's land (Transylvania, Banat, Oltenia): Dacia Traiana, the part of Decebalus's kingdom that Trajan annexed

ledger.note: 89: after Domitian's peace Decebalus is a client king of Rome. Dacia page: 'Decebalus was given the status of "king client to Rome", receiving military instructors, craftsmen and money from Rome', after the Romans 'were obligated to make peace following the defeat of Domitian by the Marcomanni, leaving the Dacians effectively independent'; Decebalus page: Domitian 'agreed to pay large sums (eight million sesterces) in annual tribute'. The Trajan's Dacian Wars page never calls Decebalus a client king and says he 'continued to oppose Rome'. Year 89 is the Marcomanni page's date for Domitian's defeat; the region is the whole kingdom as drawn. The roman-empire dossier should carry the mirror (vassal_start, counterpart dacian-kingdom, 89). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x.]

ledger.note: 101: Trajan's first war ends the client relation. 'Trajan's First Dacian War begins with a major offensive across the Danube' (101); Dacia page: 'Emperor Trajan restarted the conflicts in AD 101-102'. No page says in so many words that the client status ended; the year is the war's (the reviewer suggested confidence 3, kept at 2 for that reason). The roman-empire dossier should carry the mirror (vassal_end, counterpart dacian-kingdom, 101). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x.]

ledger.note: 101: Trajan's first Dacian War begins. 'Trajan's First Dacian War begins with a major offensive across the Danube' (101); Decebalus page: 'Trajan's force crossed the Danube in 101'. No month on the page.

region.text: 'some territories in the vicinity of the Danube' lost in 102; the Decebalus page has Decebalus attack 'the newly occupied Roman territory, probably the fortress at Banat' in 105

ledger.note: 102: Decebalus surrenders territory. 'The treaty forced him to surrender territory and engineers provided by Domitian, return equipment, accept Roman garrisons, and refrain from crossing the Danube' (Trajan's Dacian Wars page); Decebalus page: the terms 'included the loss of some territories in the vicinity of the Danube'. The year is the page's; neither page names the land, so Banat (the place the Decebalus page gives for the 'newly occupied Roman territory' attacked in 105) is the researcher's reading, confidence 2. The roman-empire dossier should carry the matching gain (counterpart dacian-kingdom, 102). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x: the contest_end note quoted 'He surrenders territory' but no loss was recorded.]

ledger.note: 102: Decebalus makes peace. 'He surrenders territory, returns equipment, accepts Roman garrisons, and agrees not to cross the Danube'; 'A Roman garrison and acting governor are established at Sarmizegetusa'; Decebalus page: peace terms were 'the loss of some territories in the vicinity of the Danube and the dismantling of his fortresses'; he kept his throne.

'With part of Dacia quelled as the Roman province Dacia Traiana' and the infobox 'Disestablished: 106 AD'; the Dacia page dates the Roman withdrawal to 271-275 under Aurelian. The north remained free as the Free Dacians and never formed a state. [Fix 2026-10-19: the region is the kingdom as it stood in 106, without Banat, which had passed to Rome in 102.]

wars.name: Domitian's Dacian War
wars.outcome: Two wars: Dacian raids on Moesia in 85 and 86, Cornelius Fuscus defeated at Tapae, Tettius Julianus's victory near Tapae in 88; Rome made peace after Domitian's defeat by the Marcomanni, Decebalus became a client king and received eight million sesterces yearly.
wars.note: Dacia page infobox: 'Domitian's Dacian War: 84-88 AD'; text '85 to 89'. The Decebalus page gives no year for Fuscus's defeat. [Fix 2026-10-19: the war now lies inside the state's life, which starts in 85 under Duras.]

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks. Three pages opened. The pages give no extent of Decebalus's kingdom, so the shape is Roman Dacia's region (the part Trajan annexed). Domitian's war is dated 85-89 on the Dacia page text (84-88 in its infobox) and its peace has no date on the Decebalus page; the Dacia page ties it to the Marcomanni's defeat of Domitian (89 on the Marcomanni page). The Free Dacians (north) 'never formed a state' (Trajan's Dacian Wars page) and are not a dossier. Wikidata id unknown. The roman-empire dossier's 105-106 contest and 106 gain name 'Dacians (Dacian kingdom)' as counterpart: this slug. The earlier Dacian kingdom is kingdom-of-burebista. Iazyges' client kingdom in Banat and Oltenia (infobox) is the sarmatians dossier's business. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: (1) the life starts in 85 under Duras (the first year the Decebalus page dates an act of the state: raids on Moesia); Decebalus's accession in 87 is a rename. The Dacia page's infobox lists Duras at 69-87 and gives no extent for those years, so 69-84 is not drawn; a fuller start would need a page on Duras's kingdom. (2) Client status added: 89-101 (Dacia page) and 102-105 (Decebalus page), both with counterpart roman-empire, confidence 2 where the reviewer proposed 3 for the 101 end: no page says that the status ended in 101. (3) The 102 loss is drawn as Banat only, from the Decebalus page's 105 sentence; the reviewer's 'Banat and Oltenia' is not supported (the Iazyge client kingdom of the Trajan page's infobox is after 106). The mirrors (roman-empire vassal events 89, 101, 102, 105 and the 102 gain of Banat) belong to the roman-empire dossier (eu-04-a). Vassal events here name the overlord as counterpart, the vassal-side reading used by kingdom-of-cappadocia; the schema text reads them from the overlord's side.]
